newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Briton tried in Moscow on drug smuggling charges.
newsitem.headline: Briton tried in Moscow on drug smuggling charges.

text.p: A British woman charged with smuggling drugs into Russia told a Moscow court on Tuesday she had bought her suitcase at Havana airport and never realised it contained almost four kg (nine pounds) of cocaine.
Russian officials discovered the drugs when they stopped 18-year-old Karen Henderson at Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport in February this year.
"I saw a big amount of white powder and I was shocked," Henderson told a Moscow court on the first day of her trial.

She said she had noticed her own suitcase was damaged as she prepared to catch a flight from the Cuban capital to Warsaw via Moscow. She said she bought a replacement case from a man she met at the airport.

Henderson is being held in Moscow's notoriously overcrowded Butyrskaya prison, which is also home to Dutch woman Suzanne Vorstenbosch. She is serving a six-year sentence after pleading guilty to smuggling cocaine into Russia.
